report.summary: Analyzed ceiling.py chunk 1 of 2: docstring claims about temporal co-change ceiling, rename-awareness, backtest-clean vs leaky arms, classification logic, and materiality thresholds. All claims checked against visible code.
risks: temporal_ceiling | medium | The function's default tasks parameter is all_tasks() which is imported and not defined in this chunk; if it returns an empty list or raises, the behavior is undefined. | Check all_tasks() definition in harness.py.

_classify | low | The def_count parameter is a callable but its contract is not fully defined in this chunk; it expects an integer return from a rel string. | Verify that def_count is always provided as _partner_counts or similar.

_AliasResolver | medium | The aliases method uses git log --follow which may be slow or fail on large repos; timeout is set but not enforced on subprocess.run. | Confirm subprocess.run respects timeout parameter.

temporal_ceiling | low | The clean_pairs and leaky_pairs are fetched with min_count=1, but the variable names suggest they are used later; if co_change_pairs returns empty list on failure, the results may be misleading. | Verify co_change_pairs error handling.
todos: Verify that all_tasks() is properly defined in harness.py and returns a list of task dicts.
Ensure that _partner_counts is used correctly as the def_count callable in _classify.
Check that subprocess.run timeout is actually enforced (it is, but only on the subprocess, not on the overall function).
Validate that co_change_pairs returns [] on failure, not None, to avoid TypeError.

handoff.purpose: Defines the temporal co-change ceiling check: classifies missed labels into REACHABLE, UNREACHABLE, STATIC_EDGE, NO_INSCOPE_DEF using rename-aware co-change counts from git history, with a clean (pre-mint) and leaky (full-history) arm.

symbols.name: CLASSES
symbols.note: Tuple of classification strings: REACHABLE, UNREACHABLE, STATIC_EDGE, NO_INSCOPE_DEF.

symbols.name: _symbol_defs
symbols.note: Reads files from repo to map symbol names to in-scope relative paths.

symbols.name: _parents_of
symbols.note: Runs git log to get parent SHAs of a given commit; returns None on failure.

symbols.name: _AliasResolver
symbols.note: Caches git log --follow alias sets per (rev, rel); counts failures.

symbols.name: _partner_counts
symbols.note: Aggregates co-change counts per partner spelling against focus aliases.

symbols.name: _classify
symbols.note: Classifies each missed label using def_count callable, static edges, and symbol definitions.

symbols.name: temporal_ceiling
symbols.note: Main entry point: computes both arms of the ceiling over tasks.

claims.text: The independent_diff corpus has miss tasks: minted ``must_include`` labels the current slice does not contain.
claims.why: This claim refers to the external corpus independent_diff, which is not defined or referenced in this chunk.

claims.text: The "temporal" hypothesis says a co-change tier (files that repeatedly change together with no static import edge -- ``structcore.churn.co_change_pairs``) could recover them.
claims.why: co_change_pairs is imported and used in temporal_ceiling; the classification STATIC_EDGE separates files that already have a static edge.

claims.text: Before any slice-side enrichment is built, this module measures the CEILING of that hypothesis: for every missed label, is ANY in-scope file defining that symbol a co-change partner of the task's focus file at all?
claims.why: temporal_ceiling calls _classify which checks if any defining file's co-change count >= min_count.

claims.text: If a label's defining file is not even a partner, no enrichment built on these pairs can ever surface it -- so this number is a hard upper bound on what a temporal tier could add, measured for the price of a git log instead of a build.
claims.why: This claim about the 'hard upper bound' is conceptual and not directly checkable against code; the code computes the ceiling but does not assert it is a hard upper bound.

claims.text: BACKTEST-CLEAN, OR THE NUMBER IS A TAUTOLOGY. Every minted task records the commit it came from (``minted_at_sha``), and that commit CO-CHANGED the focus and the label sources -- that is what minting means. Counting it would let the eval "predict" a commit from that same commit's own data. The clean arm therefore computes pairs over ``git log <minted_at_sha>^`` -- history strictly before the mint (first-parent semantics; merge SHAs are flagged in the row rather than silently half-counted).
claims.why: In temporal_ceiling, clean_pairs = co_change_pairs(repo, min_count=1, rev=rev) where rev = f"{sha}^" if has_rev else None, and has_rev is derived from _parents_of which uses git log --format=%P -1 sha (first-parent semantics).

claims.text: The LEAKY arm (full history) is computed alongside on purpose: the gap between the two arms is the measured size of the self-prediction artifact.
claims.why: leaky_pairs = co_change_pairs(repo, min_count=1) is computed without a rev, i.e., full history.

claims.text: RENAME-AWARE, BECAUSE THE ADVERSARIAL PASS PROVED IT MATTERS. Git numstat paths carry each commit's OWN spelling; a file renamed since (this repo's agent_env -> daedalus rebrand renamed 93 files at once) leaves its pre-rename co-changes invisible to an exact-rel match, understating the ceiling. So this module resolves every focus/defining file to its full historical alias set (``git log --follow``) and sums co-change counts across spellings BEFORE applying ``min_count``.
claims.why: _AliasResolver uses git log --follow to get all historical names; _partner_counts sums counts across all aliases of the focus before thresholding. Both arms fetch with min_count=1 and then apply the threshold in _classify.

claims.text: MEASURED CLOSE (2026-07-21, agent_env corpus, 7 miss tasks / 43 missed labels; rename-blind first pass corrected by the Nemesis rename-map recount, then reproduced by this module): clean ceiling at min_count=2 = 1/43 = 2.3% (a single label, ``_dispatch``: genuine verifier<->ollama coupling crossing the rebrand); min_count=1 adds nothing further; leaky full-history arm = 6/43 at min_count=2 and 42/43 at min_count=1 -- the self-prediction artifact, nearly total at the permissive setting.
claims.why: This is a historical measurement result; the code does not contain these numbers or assertions about them.

claims.text: Structural context that bounds any future hope here: 41 of 43 missed labels sit on focus files BORN AT THEIR MINT COMMIT (zero pre-mint history -- test files created by the very feature commit they were minted from), so for them clean unreachability is structural truth under ANY enrichment; the remaining NO_INSCOPE_DEF label (``_py_maps``) is a stale label whose definition the mint commit itself deleted.
claims.why: This is a historical observation; the code does not contain these numbers or assertions about them.

claims.text: Conclusion: the "temporal class" of misses was predominantly the mint commit predicting itself, and slice-side co-change enrichment was NOT built (design NO-GO'd on this measurement; 1 recoverable label is below any sane build threshold).
claims.why: This is a design decision conclusion; not checkable against the code.

claims.text: THE REOPEN CONDITION (with a materiality floor -- a lone recoverable label must not reopen a core-API build): reopen the enrichment lane only when a re-run on a grown corpus reports a clean, rename-aware ceiling at min_count >= 2 that clears ``REOPEN_MIN_SHARE`` of scored labels OR touches ``REOPEN_MIN_TASKS`` distinct tasks.
claims.why: The reopen condition is described but not implemented in this chunk; it is a policy statement.

claims.text: Caveat to carry: a corpus whose focus files are born at their mint commits (like today's) can NEVER trip this regardless of how real temporal coupling is elsewhere -- the zero generalizes weakly, so re-run it as the corpus grows rather than citing today's close as permanent.
claims.why: This is a caveat about the reopen condition; not checkable against the code.

claims.text: Per the package contract, imports only structcore's stable public API plus sibling eval modules. Read-only: never writes the store, the baseline, or any file. ADVISORY, like every eval number -- see harness.py's guardrail.
claims.why: Imports are from structcore (churn, index, languages, parse) and sibling eval modules (harness, tasks). No file writes are performed in this chunk; all operations are read-only (reading files, git commands).

claims.text: symbol name -> set of IN-SCOPE rels defining a unit with that name, from the current worktree (the same text the slice would emit).
claims.why: The function reads files from the repo (current worktree) and extracts units using extract_units, collecting symbol names and their defining rels.

claims.text: Parent SHAs of ``sha``, or None when git/the ref is unavailable -- the probe that distinguishes "no pre-mint history exists" (root commit / unknown ref / no git) from "history exists but shows no coupling", which ``co_change_pairs``'s []-on-failure contract deliberately does not.
claims.why: The function returns None on subprocess error or non-zero return code; otherwise returns the stdout split (list of parent SHAs). It distinguishes failure from empty history (list could be empty for root commit, but docstring says None for failure).

claims.text: Historical alias sets (``git log --follow --name-only``) for the small set of rels the ceiling actually inspects (focus + defining files), cached per (rev, rel). A probe failure degrades to ``{rel}`` (rename-blind for that file, i.e. an UNDER-statement of the ceiling) and is COUNTED -- the render surfaces a non-zero failure count rather than letting a degraded instrument print an authoritative-looking zero.
claims.why: On failure, self.failures is incremented, and the cache stores {rel} (the original rel). So it degrades to a singleton set, which is rename-blind.

claims.text: Co-change count per partner SPELLING against ANY alias of the focus. ``pairs`` must come from ``co_change_pairs(min_count=1)``: unification has to happen BEFORE thresholding, or two spellings of one real pair (count 1 each) die at min_count=2 that they genuinely clear together -- the exact rename-blindness the adversarial pass caught.
claims.why: The function takes focus_aliases (a set of all historical spellings) and sums counts for any partner that appears in any pair where one side is a focus alias and the other is not. It uses raw counts from pairs (which are at min_count=1). The note about thresholding after summing is followed: _classify applies min_count after _partner_counts.

claims.text: ``def_count(rel) -> int`` returns the rename-unified co-change count of a defining file with the focus under the arm being classified.
claims.why: In _classify, def_count is called with a defining file's rel and compared to min_count. The docstring describes the contract; the code uses it as such.

claims.text: Both arms of the ceiling over every miss task in ``tasks`` (default: ``all_tasks()``). Read-only; returns a plain dict, renders via ``render_ceiling``. Errored / focus-withheld tasks are excluded from the denominator and reported by id -- same discipline as the harness.
claims.why: The function defaults tasks to all_tasks(). It catches exceptions (ValueError, OSError) and excludes tasks with 'error' in row or focus_withheld. It returns a plain dict (the return statement is not shown but implied). The docstring says it is read-only; no writes are performed.

claims.text: min_count=1 fetch on BOTH arms: rename-unification must sum counts across spellings before the threshold is applied (see _partner_counts).
claims.why: Both clean_pairs and leaky_pairs are fetched with min_count=1. The threshold is applied later in _classify via def_count (which presumably uses _partner_counts or similar).

observations.what: The function _parents_of uses git log --format=%P -1 sha, which returns parent SHAs separated by spaces. The split() will treat multiple parents (merge commit) as separate strings, but the docstring says 'first-parent semantics' and merge SHAs are flagged. However, the code does not flag merge SHAs; it just returns all parents. The docstring claim about 'flagged in the row' is not implemented in this chunk.

In temporal_ceiling, the variable rev is set to f"{sha}^" if has_rev else None. This uses first-parent by default (the ^ suffix follows first parent). However, _parents_of returns all parents, and has_rev is True if any parent exists. For merge commits, the first parent is used, which matches the docstring. But the docstring also says 'merge SHAs are flagged in the row' -- no such flagging is visible in this chunk.
The _classify function sorts defs with sorted(defs) before checking any(def_count(d) >= min_count). Sorting is unnecessary for the logic but harmless.
The module docstring claims 'Read-only: never writes the store, the baseline, or any file.' This is true for the visible code; no file writes are present.
The constants REOPEN_MIN_SHARE and REOPEN_MIN_TASKS are defined but not used in this chunk. They are presumably used in render_ceiling or elsewhere.
